unmapped_findings: Room-temperature fracture mode of Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C is transgranular cleavage (TGC) (Table 2, Fig. 4d).
Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C has higher matrix hardness but lower yield stress in compression than Fe-15Al-2Ta-1C (b0023).

In room-temperature tension, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C (Fig. 3, curve 4) showed linear elastic loading followed by abrupt load drop, peaking around the 500 MPa gridline; yield stress in tension and total elongation are reported as '-' in Table 2.

At elevated temperatures, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C (Nb-containing) shows the highest strength among Fe-15Al-based alloys at all tested temperatures; its compressive yield stress decreases monotonically with temperature with no yield stress anomaly (Fig. 5, b0038).
At 800 °C, Fe-15Al-2Nb-1C exhibits tension-compression asymmetry (compression yield stress higher than tension), consistent with all investigated alloys (Fig. 8, b0040).
The Nb- and Ta-containing Fe-15Al-based alloys show the highest strengthening effects in room-temperature compression (b0025).
